title: LLM as Attention-Informed NTM and Topic Modeling as long-input Generation: Interpretability and long-Context Capability
subcategory: white-box attention structures and black-box long-context topic modelling
task: Recovering topic structures from LLMs and topic modelling with long-context LLMs
problem: It is unclear whether LLMs implicitly perform topic modelling and how black-box LLMs can give testable topic-document correspondences.
architecture: White-box: aggregate top-K token attention of Qwen3-8B to fragment level to recover document-topic and topic-word distributions. Black-box: the whole corpus is given as one long input; each topic is generated with label, summary, keywords and representative titles; post-generation signal compensation assigns documents with hybrid lexical/dense retrieval (BGE-M3).
llm_or_encoder: Qwen3-8B (white-box); DeepSeek-V3.1, Qwen3.5, Llama-4, GPT-5.3, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini-3.1 (black-box); BGE-M3

datasets.name: NYT
datasets.details: New York Times; 48 documents for the white-box study

key_results: White-box: 26 of 48 documents correctly assigned (54.17%), with an upper bound of about 75% because 12 documents fit no topic.
Black-box assignment accuracy 69.7%-94.4% for long-context LLMs vs 19.2%-31.4% for NTMs and clustering models.
NPMI of LLM topics (0.1113-0.1886) is lower than ECRTM (0.6110) and DecTM (0.5542).
strengths: Connects LLM attention with NTM-style distributions; evaluates current long-context LLMs directly.

limitations.text: Attention dispersion bias for later-generated topics; white-box study limited to 4,000 tokens and 48 documents; retrieval adds cost; LLMs may not use long contexts fully.
Topic quality partly judged by LLMs, which may favour LLM-generated topics; single dataset.
